root.note: The Arabic word itself is generally taken from Persian dēvān, ‘register’.

stages.meaning: register; office of state; customs house

history: La dogana is the office where goods are checked and duties are paid, and the word comes from the Arab world. Arabic dīwān was a register, and by extension the office where the registers were kept. Italian port cities such as Venice and Genoa traded with the Arab East, and their merchants brought the word home in the Middle Ages. It entered Latin documents as doana and settled in Italian as dogana. French has douane and Spanish aduana, from the same source. The same Arabic word also gave Italian divano, because a council sat on cushioned benches along the wall, and English divan. You will meet dogana at an airport or at a post office when you receive a parcel from outside the EU.
historyEinfach: Dogana comes from Arabic dīwān, a ‘register’ or an office. Italian merchants learned it from Arab traders. It means the place where goods are checked and taxes are paid. The same Arabic word also gave Italian divano (sofa).

elsewhere.text: French took the word from the same source in the Middle Ages. Spanish aduana has the Arabic article al- in front: al-dīwān.
